content: Concerning negation the following papers are of interest: BIBREF20 analyze the grammatical knowledge captured by BERT. In a case study, they test for correct licensing environments for negative polarity items. They study a set of classifiers distinguishing between grammatically correct and incorrect sentences. We take a different approach by focusing on factual knowledge stored in negated statements. Grammatically correct statements can still be factually false (e.g., “General relativity, Newton develop”).
